WHAT: a tiny solid-state relay. An LED on the input side switches a MOSFET on the output side, so the output is electrically isolated from the Pico, with no moving contacts. We use it to switch resistors and the SHUT DOWN line.
CHECK: type "1 Form A" (normally OPEN, one switch); not "Form B" (normally closed) and not 2 Form A. Load voltage rating ≥ 60 V (we switch ≤ 16 V). Load current ≥ 100 mA. LED current: the board gives about 6 mA (3.3 V, 330 Ω), so the datasheet's "trigger LED current IFT" must be well under 6 mA (typically 1–3 mA). On-resistance a few ohms to about 30 Ω is fine. column15: Check leakage near 3.3 V.

WHAT: a protection diode that conducts only above a set voltage and clamps spikes (static, coil kick) on the DUT terminals.
CHECK: suffix "CA" = bidirectional (needed: the node can swing negative). Stand-off voltage (VRWM) 5.0 V: it must NOT conduct below 5 V, because the node normally sits between about −3.3 V and +3.3 V. Breakdown voltage about 6.4 V. Check the leakage at 3.3 V (should be small). Package SMA (DO-214AC) for SMAJ, SMB for SMBJ: match the footprint.

column15: Used on both clamp modules (CH-R2 and CH-PU). NOT the PMEG3050EP.

WHAT: two small fast diodes in one package, used as the clamp at the ADC input (one diode to 3.3 V, one to ground) so a spike cannot reach the chip. They sit on a small plug-in module.
CHECK: exactly "BAT54S" (the two diodes in SERIES: pin 1 = anode of D1, pin 2 = cathode of D2, pin 3 = the middle point). BAT54A (common anode), BAT54C (common cathode) and BAT54 (single) look the same but are wired differently, and would make the clamp wrong. Forward voltage about 0.3 V, leakage at 25 V in the microamp range. Package SOT-23. Do NOT use a big low-drop Schottky like the PMEG3050EP: it leaked and falsified the readings.

WHAT: protects the pickup input from voltage spikes.

column12: MCP6022, any dual RR op-amp (3.3 V)
column16:
WHAT: two amplifiers in one chip. We use them as unity buffers: one makes the 1.65 V reference, one drives the signal into the Pico.
CHECK: dual (not the single MCP6001). Rail-to-rail input AND output, works at 3.3 V (supply 1.8–6 V). Pins: 1 OUT A, 2 IN− A, 3 IN+ A, 4 V−, 5 IN+ B, 6 IN− B, 7 OUT B, 8 V+. Package SOIC-8 (suffix /SN). Ordinary op-amps (LM358, TL072) do not work at 3.3 V.

WHAT: four electronic on/off switches in one chip; three select the pickup input range.
CHECK: "74HC4066" (the HC family works at 3.3 V). Do not buy the old "CD4066B": its resistance is too high at 3.3 V. On-resistance about 100–200 Ω at 3.3 V (fine). Package SOIC-14. It is the 4066 (4 switches), not 4051 (8-way mux) or 4053.

column12: MCP6542-I/SN (not the LM393: its input range is too small at 3.3 V)
column16:
WHAT: compares the pickup signal with a threshold and gives a clean digital edge for timing the pulses.
CHECK: dual comparator, SOIC-8, supply down to 3.3 V or lower, and input range that includes BOTH rails (rail-to-rail inputs), because the thresholds sit around 1.3–2.0 V and the signal swings 0.15–3.15 V. Push-pull output is easiest (open-drain types need the 10 kΩ pull-ups fitted). Response time under 1 µs. Standard pinout: 1 OUT A, 2 IN− A, 3 IN+ A, 4 GND, 5 IN+ B, 6 IN− B, 7 OUT B, 8 V+.
CORRECTION: the LM393 is NOT suitable here. Its inputs only work up to about 1.5 V below the supply (about 1.8 V at 3.3 V), which our thresholds and signal exceed. I removed it from the alternatives.

WHAT: a chip that turns two numbers from the Pico into two precise voltages (the comparator thresholds).
CHECK: "MCP4822" is the 12-bit dual one (MCP4812 is 10-bit, MCP4802 is 8-bit, all look alike). SPI interface, internal 2.048 V reference, supply 2.7–5.5 V, package SOIC-8 (suffix /SN).

column15: The pickup voltage is across it: must be ≥ 350 V.
column16:
WHAT: the same kind of solid-state relay, but for the pickup input: when open, the full pickup voltage sits across it.
CHECK: 1 Form A, load voltage ≥ 350 V. Load current: a pickup at 100 V into the 1 kΩ load is 100 mA peak, so look for a continuous rating of at least 100–120 mA and a peak/pulse rating higher than that. If it is lower, tell me and we will add a series resistor. LED trigger current under 5 mA (we give 6 mA). SOP-4.

WHAT: a power transistor used as an electronic switch for the 12 V supply (reverse-polarity protection and the ARM switch).
CHECK: P-channel (not N-channel: IRF540 and similar are N-channel, wrong). Drain-source voltage −55 V or better, current ≥ 10 A (the part is 74 A), on-resistance ≤ 0.03 Ω at VGS = −10 V, gate-source limit ±20 V, gate threshold about −2 to −4 V. Package TO-220 (not the D2PAK "IRF4905S" variant). Pins on the TO-220: gate, drain, source (check against the footprint).

CHECK: coil voltage 12 V DC, coil current under about 40 mA (a 2N7000 drives it; a 120 mW coil is about 360 Ω), contact rating ≥ 10 A at 12–24 V DC (the DC rating, not only AC). One normally-open contact is needed: an SPDT (Form C) works, using the NO contact. DC coil, non-latching. PIN SPACING: compare the datasheet's pin drawing with the footprint before the PCB order.

WHAT: a small transistor that switches the relay coil.
CHECK: N-channel, 60 V, 200 mA or more (the coil needs about 33 mA), gate threshold about 0.8–3 V. IMPORTANT: the pin order of the TO-92 case differs between 2N7000 (source-gate-drain) and BS170 (drain-gate-source); check the datasheet against the footprint.

Supply 3.0–5.5 V on both sides, package SOIC-8 (suffix ARZ), isolation 2.5 kV. The TI ISO1541 is a similar part: check that both lines are bidirectional.

column16: Same part as the 0x48 one (see that row). The address is set by wiring the ADDR pin to 3V3_P on the board, not by the part number.

WHAT: turns a number into a precise voltage (0–3.3 V). Two of them set the pulse amplitude.

CHECK: dual "TL072" (TL071 is single, wrong), supply range up to ±18 V (36 V total; we use 17 V), SOIC-8, pins: 4 V−, 8 V+. Output reaches about 1.5 V short of the supplies.

WHAT: an electronic selector that connects one of several voltages to the output. It creates the trigger pulse by switching between +level, −level and ground.
CHECK: the "B-series" CD4052B (or HEF4052B), dual 4-channel, with a separate negative supply pin VEE (pin 7), supply range 3–18 V (we apply 12 V − (−5 V) = 17 V, close to the 18 V limit). The 74HC4052 is NOT suitable (its supply limit is only about 10 V). Package SOIC-16. It is the 4052 (dual 4:1), not the CD4051 (8:1) or CD4053 (triple 2:1).

column15: Use the TO-92 footprint on the PCB.
column16:
WHAT: makes a steady 5 V from the 12 V rail (100 mA).
CHECK: "L78L05" = 5 V (78L09 = 9 V, 79L05 = negative, LM317 = adjustable: all wrong). Maximum input ≥ 16 V (the part allows about 30 V), output 4.8–5.2 V, 100 mA. TO-92 package. WARNING: the TO-92 pin order of this regulator (output, ground, input) differs from a 2N7000: use the datasheet.
Same as the 78L05 but 9 V output. CHECK: "L78L09", input maximum ≥ 16 V, TO-92. Only used for the optional ±9 V version.

WHAT: makes 3.3 V from the 5 V for the 12 V-side logic.
CHECK: fixed 3.3 V version ("-3.3"), maximum input voltage at least 5.5 V (AP2112K and MCP1700 allow about 6 V: do NOT feed them 12 V), current ≥ 100 mA, package SOT-23-5 (AP2112K) or SOT-23 (MCP1700). Pin order differs between the two: check the footprint.

WHAT: turns +5 V into about −5 V using two capacitors, to supply the negative side of the op-amp and multiplexer.
CHECK: ICL7660 / TC7660 / MAX1044 are compatible 8-pin inverters. Input voltage 1.5–10 V (we feed 5 V; the 9 V option is close to the limit; the "A" version accepts 12 V). Output current ≥ 20 mA. Package SOIC-8. Needs two 10 µF capacitors. Pins: 2 CAP+, 3 GND, 4 CAP−, 5 VOUT, 8 V+.

Package SOP-4 (4 pins). Isolation ≥ 1.5 kV. It must switch DC: avoid TRIAC / "phototriac" output types.
